newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-ROVERS POISED TO SINK PIRATES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ROVERS POISED TO SINK PIRATES.

text.p: South Africa's Orlando Pirates face humiliating defeat in the first round of the African Champions' Cup at the weekend.
The popular Soweto club, known in South Africa as the "people's team", broke a 12-year stranglehold by clubs from Arab-speaking north Africa when they won the top African club title in 1995.
It was the first time since 1983 that a team from sub-Sahara Africa had taken the Champions' Cup and signaled a change in the continent's soccer's powerbase.
Last year, Pirates lost in a penalty shootout at the quarter-final stage in defence of their title but were among the trophy favourites again this year.
But now they face elimination by Roma Rovers, a student team from the tiny mountain kingdom of Lesotho.
Pirates have a slender 1-0 lead to take to Maseru for Sunday's second leg and will face a country bent on upsetting the main attraction from their powerful neighbours.
Rovers, playing in the cup for the first time, scored five goals at home in the preliminary round and will be better placed to used the uneven bounce and difficult conditions of the Sesotho stadium.
Also in their favour is the fact that Pirates remain rudderless after coach Augusto Palacios was attacked by angry fans earlier this month after they lost a league match.
Rovers are not the only small side with a chance of a rare upset this weekend.

Notwane from Botswana are in line to reach the second round for the first time when they host Primiero de Agosto of Angola in Gaborone on Sunday after drawing 1-1 in Luanda in the first leg two weeks ago.
In the African Cup Winners' Cup, Senegalese second division club US Goreenne take a 1-0 lead to Algeria for their second leg against Mouloudia Oran.
Confederation of African Football (CAF) Cup holders Kawkab Marrakesh travel to Senegal with a slender one-goal lead against ASC la Linguere.
